title: Technical English — Course 5, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 3

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the report review take place?
tasks.audioText: The technical writing tutor will review an integrated report on Thursday at one. Students should bring the sample inspection record and trend chart. The class will combine a measured result with a short explanation of its context and limitations. The tutor will ask students to distinguish evidence from interpretation and to reference each source clearly.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which two records are needed for the maintenance handover exercise?
tasks.audioText: The technical writing tutor will review an integrated report on Thursday at one. Students should bring the sample inspection record and trend chart. The class will combine a measured result with a short explanation of its context and limitations. The tutor will ask students to distinguish evidence from interpretation and to reference each source clearly.
options: The sample inspection record and trend chart

tasks.prompt: An integrated technical report may combine measurements, inspection findings and trend data. Each source should be identified so that a reader can trace where the information came from. The report should explain how the sources relate, but it must not imply that correlation proves causation. Conclusions should be proportionate to the evidence, and any limitation should be stated clearly. Reading 1. Why should each information source be identified?
options: To show that all measurements were taken at the same time
To prove that one source caused another
So readers can trace where information came from
To remove the need to explain limitations

tasks.prompt: What should a report avoid implying?
options: That all sources are equally reliable
That one trend predicts every future event
That a report must include every available measurement

tasks.prompt: The conclusions ___ to the strength of the available evidence.
Choose TWO qualities of an integrated technical report.
options: Claims that exceed the available data

tasks.prompt: A conclusion that is supported by available information is described as evidence-___.
Two trends occur at the same time, but causation has not been established. What should you write?
options: One trend definitely causes the other.
The trends coincide, but the available evidence does not establish a causal relationship.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of integrated technical reporting in a logical order.
options: Compare the information and identify limitations
Write conclusions that match the evidence
correctOrder: Compare the information and identify limitations
Write conclusions that match the evidence

tasks.prompt: Write 100–120 words explaining how to combine inspection findings and trend data in a technical report without overstating conclusions.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total. Score each criterion 0–2: (1) Inspection evidence — 2: accurately summarises relevant findings and their source; 1: partial; 0: absent. (2) Trend data — 2: explains how comparable trend data adds context; 1: partial; 0: absent or misinterpreted. (3) Limits and conclusions — 2: distinguishes evidence from inference and states limitations without overstating certainty; 1: partial; 0: unsupported conclusion. (4) English — 2: coherent technical-report language and accurate inspection/reliability vocabulary; 1: errors but meaning clear; 0: meaning frequently unclear.
